Synopsis:
Right outside of the abandonned chapel of Selune you encounter a few bandits arguing among themselves. They are rightfully surprise to see you get out of the ruins and worried about the fate of their friend inside.

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_Outside_BanditBackInteraction_Spotted.json: You’ve just emerged from an old, neglected chapel/tomb of Selûne where you and your party reached a small sanctum with a worn statue and an unreadable bronze plaque — the group currently lacks a reliable way to translate the inscription. Outside the ruin a small gang of bandits, led by Gimblebock, argue among themselves; they thought the crypt was theirs, have people posted inside, and are suddenly alarmed to see you coming out. They’re worried about the fate of their friend left in the chapel and shift quickly between bluster and panic, accusing you of poaching their loot or attacking outright. Depending on how you respond (threats, demands, or violence) they may back down and flee or escalate into a fight.

The lines are a post‑raid debate over whether looting the dead was justified and what to do with the relics, not a detailed replay of the fight. Because this is a party voicebark, any companion might speak the lines and they reflect the party’s collective action and attitude rather than a named NPC’s fixed stance.

The player can convince them to clear off via lies or threats, or else is forced to fight them. A gnome named Gimblebock is in charge of this group, with his underlings, Quelanna and/or Taman, chiming in at points with their concerns.
- CHA_Outside_Bandit_Melee_01_Dead.json: Gimblebock is the dead leader of the bandits currently looting the ruined chapel near where the player first woke; you have used Speak with Dead to raise his corpse. He can only truthfully speak about things he knew when alive, and his replies will be cryptic, fragmentary, and unable to sustain long explanations — expect short clues rather than full narratives. If he recognizes the questioner as his killer he will refuse to answer. The spirit will answer at most five questions before falling silent, and off‑screen facts likely to matter are the chapel looting, his role as bandit leader, and any recent encounters the party had there.

Outside, a small gang of bandits led by Gimblebock is arguing; they believed the crypt was theirs and say they had people posted inside. The bandits are startled and suspicious to see you, swinging between bluster and panic as they worry about a friend left in the chapel and accuse you of poaching loot or attacking them.
